title: Spoken Once, Heard Twice
notes: The chunk teaches the dual-reading principle cleanly from Jeremiah’s almond vision through the woman/fire chain to Genesis 3:15 and Revelation 12, keeping density, assertion, and law-positive voice. Scripture blocks, sym: links, and Hebrew letter claims are intact and free of AI stock diction. Five author-prose sentences open with And or But, violating house style. One elliptical title sentence (“is one”) needs a clarifying noun for readability. No director-cue list items, quote typos, or factual mismatches appear.

proposals.old: And John reopens the garden by name: the dragon of his vision is __“that old *serpent*”__ (Revelation 12:9); the woman travails and bears the __“*man child*, who was to rule all nations”__ (Revelation 12:5); and the serpent's ancient enmity finds its stated target — __“the dragon… went to make war with *the remnant of her seed*, which keep the commandments of God”__ (Revelation 12:17).
